posts.cooked: I just want to confirm how this works.  Let's say Nightmist is in the Ruins of Atlantis (it seems like a logical place for her to go).  Pillars of Hercules is played, and then she plays Mistbound on the villain deck, or vice versa.  When it comes to the start of her next turn, if Pillars is still in play, which happens - Pillars tries to play a villain card, but Mistbound prevents this; or Misbound wears off, then Pillars plays a villain card?  Does card play order determine this resolution?  I kind of feel as though "until the start of your next turn" events should wear off immediately upon the turn starting, rather than going into the same queue as @SOT triggers.  But perhaps that's just me having an impulse that isn't in line with the game rules.

posts.name: phantaskippy
posts.cooked:
Until the start of your turn should not include any of the start of your turn.  It would end as your turn started.  So I would think the villain deck would be able to play a card.

So the order should go:

End of previous turn

Mistbound wears off

Start of Nightmist's turn

 

However, the word until in common usage often means up to and including, and while less correct it is common.

Under that interpretation it would wear off during your start of turn, and would be decided by the order the cards entered play.

 

This would be a good official question, as there are more situations with this language that can occur, like Adept boosting his own damage and infection.

I would decide on how you want to deal with it and keep constant with that until an official ruling is given.

I of course prefer it wearing off before the start of turn, because I dislike increased card order bookkeeping.

There is a difference between the time a card enters play and the time it activates, I think it could be possible that there could be an effect that ends right before the start of turn.

There is timing inside of the start of your turn.  Your start of turn ends after the previous turns end of turn ends.  Multiple effects can resolve during your start of turn, and then it ends when it is time for your Play a Card action.

But until you actually get to your Start of turn Phase, the trigger is not met. I highly doubt the intent is "right before the start of your turn, destroy this card" you know? 

"start of turn" is a sub-sect of your turn, it does not get broken up into smaller sub-sects. The Start of Turn phase ends before you start resolving effects. For Villains that flip at the start of turn, like the Rat, you don't flip him (due to SoT effect) then procceed to resolve the SoT effect on his flip side. Why? Because the SoT phase had already come and gone and you are just resolving the effects that triggered as a result of hitting SoT. 

So the "until" wording really reads "Until you get to the start of your turn phase…" not "right before you get to the start of your turn phase". The latter is a very wonky interpretation of how phases work in this game. Nothing else works that way.

posts.name: phantaskippy
posts.cooked:
This is awesome, I agree on how you get there, just disagree with the result, it must be opposite day.

The start of turn is a moment that occurs, not a phase.  That moment can be subdivided into timing for simultaneous effects (just explaining my previous post a bit better)

An until worded effect does not have an end trigger.

Cards say "At the start of your turn, destroy this card."  That is a trigger.  It gives a timing trigger and an effect, Effects that activate for a specific time simply stop, they don't trigger a cancelling of the effect or something like that, they just stop.

To me they would work like Imbued fire's effect no longer effecting damage that was suddenly changed from fire to something else.  There is no timing, no trigger, it just doesn't effect things anymore.

When the start of your turn occurs the effect would no longer be active.
